answer: A rendering market offering velvet textures and umber dune scenes could allocate free trials per attested hardware security module, not per agent name. Each module signs a fresh server nonce, and a registry enforces one trial quota per certified device. Creating aliases then adds no quota: an attacker must acquire more genuine devices or compromise their keys. Hardware purchases raise the cost, but rented device farms, manufacturer trust and exclusion of users without supported hardware limit this defense.
